name: Harvest Guardian
body:
Harvest Guardians are the elite of Demeter’s champions. These warrior farmers are among the highest ranking members of Demeter’s temple and they hold positions of authority on various councils and courts.

Background: Harvest Guardians have dedicated their lives to the service of the Greek goddess Demeter, embracing her teachings of agriculture, fertility, and the cycles of life.

Emerging from various walks of life, these warriors are united by their shared reverence for the goddess and their unwavering commitment to preserving the bountiful harvest. From a young age, they are immersed in the wisdom of Demeter, learning the sacred rituals and practices that honor the earth and ensure its fruitful abundance. Through rigorous training, they cultivate their skills in both combat and agricultural arts, embodying the virtues of nurturing care, resilience, and a deep connection to the natural world.

Harvest Guardians have an enduring and storied history with the cult of Demeter. Many have been acolytes and initiates, dedicating themselves to the goddess’s teachings and participating in the rituals that sustain the cycles of life and growth. Over the years, they have forged profound connections within the cult and the wider community, acting as pillars of support and guardians of agricultural knowledge. Their wisdom, garnered from generations past, fuels their dedication to safeguarding the prosperity of the land and the welfare of those who rely on its nourishment.

Adventures: As steadfast protectors of agriculture and fertility, Harvest Guardians are entrusted with the weightiest responsibilities.

When grave threats loom over the harvest or when the delicate balance of nature is endangered, a Harvest Guardian heeds the call to action. Driven by their unyielding devotion to Demeter and their profound connection to the cycles of life, Harvest Guardians embark on perilous adventures to restore harmony and ensure the sustenance of all. Whether battling against natural disasters, combating forces that disrupt the fertility of the land, or venturing into unknown territories to retrieve lost agricultural wisdom, Harvest Guardians rise to the occasion, guided by their unshakable faith in Demeter’s benevolence and their determination to protect the sanctity of the harvest.

Requirements

To qualify to become a Harvest Guardian, a character must fulfill all the following criteria.

Base Attack Bonus: +8
Skills: Knowledge (nature) 8 ranks, Knowledge (religion) 8 ranks
Special: Familial Bond and Lay on Hands class abilities
Class Skills

The Harvest Guardian’s class skills are Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), and Sense Motive (Wis)

Skill Ranks at Each Level: 4 + Int modifier

Hit Die: d10

Table: The Harvest Guardian
Level	Base Attack	Fort	Ref	Will	Special	Spells per Day
1	+1	+1	+0	+1	Aura of safety, familial bond, lay on hands	+1 level of existing class
2	+2	+1	+1	+1	Mercy	+1 level of existing class
3	+3	+2	+1	+2	Familial bond +1 time per day	+1 level of existing class
4	+4	+2	+1	+2	Aura of sacrifice, familial bond	+1 level of existing class
5	+5	+3	+2	+3	Champion’s aura, Familial bond +1 time per day	+1 level of existing class
Class Features

Harvest Guardians have the following class features.

Aura of Safety (Su)

At 1st level, a Champion of the First Protector gains immunity to hexes and curse spells or abilities. Each ally within 10 feet of her gains a +4 morale bonus on saving throws against hexes or curses. This ability functions only while the champion is conscious, not if she is unconscious or dead.

Lay on Hands (Su)

The Harvest Guardian’s class levels are added to their Champion of Demeter levels when determining the number of uses and amount of healing granted by their Lay on Hands ability.

Mercy (Su)

At 2nd level, a Harvest Guardian adds the following mercies to the list of those that can be selected.

Amputated: The champion’s lay on hands also acts as regenerate, but only for the purposes of regrowing severed body members, broken bones, and ruined organs. The champion must have the injured mercy before she can select this mercy.
Blinded: The target is no longer blinded.
Confused: The target is no longer confused.
Cursed: The champion’s lay on hands ability also acts as remove curse, using the champion’s level as the caster level.
Deafened: The target is no longer deafened.
Ensorcelled: The champion’s lay on hands also acts as dispel magic, using the champion’s level as her caster level (maximum 20).
Exhausted: The target is no longer exhausted. The champion must have the fatigue mercy before selecting this mercy.
Frightened: The target is no longer frightened. The champion must have the shaken mercy before selecting this mercy.
Injured: The target gains fast healing 3 for a number of rounds equal to 1/2 the champion’s character level.
Nauseated: The target is no longer nauseated. The champion must have the sickened mercy before selecting this mercy.
Paralyzed: The target is no longer paralyzed.
Petrified: The champion’s Lay on Hands ability also acts as stone to flesh, but only for the purpose of removing the petrified condition from a creature.
Poisoned: The champion’s lay on hands ability also acts as neutralize poison, using the champion’s character level as the caster level.
Restorative: The target heals 1d4 points of ability damage from a single ability score of the champion’s choosing. The champion must have the enfeebled mercy before selecting this mercy.
Stunned: The target is no longer stunned.
Familial Bond (Sp)

At 2nd level, the Natural Armor bonus imparted by the Harvest Guardian’s Familial Bond ability increases by +1 and it increases another 1 point when the Harvest Guardian reaches 4th level. At 3rd level and again at 5th level, a Harvest Guardian gains one additional daily use of her Familial Bond ability.

Aura of Sacrifice (Su)

At 4th level, a Champion of the First Protector can take damage in place of an ally. When an ally within 30 feet of the champion takes damage, the champion can use an immediate action to negate a number of points of damage equal to her Charisma modifier. The champion then takes that amount of damage. The Champion of the First Protector can apply any Damage Reduction she has to this damage, potentially negating the damage to herself.

Champion’s Aura (Su)

At 5th level, the champion’s zeal is so inspiring that it affects all around her. The ranges of all of the champion’s auras increase by 30 feet.
